texts: good. the bare plural becomes a fireable per-sky-cat rule, the molting sky-cat is recorded as the one undergoing the molt, and "late summer" rides the event's time slot.

mixed: nothing is lost and the rule fires, but this time the molting sky-cat is recorded as a volitional doer rather than as the one undergoing the molt — and the otherwise identical "late summer" sentence above got it right, so this is a translator slip rather than anything wrong with your wording. No rewrite would fix it reliably; keep the sentence as written and have it re-parsed.

mixed: the group-level event covers everything — the gathering, the morning slot, the daily cycle and the molting-season window — but the extra per-collector rule the parser adds carries none of the three time restrictions, so it claims each collector gathers the fallen feathers at any hour of any season. Making the subject a single collective body removes that split entirely: "Tessa Brae's collecting crew gathers the fallen feathers each morning during the molting season." If you need each collector to stay individually queryable, keep your plural wording and have it re-parsed instead — the fault is in the rule the translator built, not in your sentence.

good. the of-phrase ties the feathers to sky-cats, the ground-feather restriction rides in the rule's premise, and both the lanterns warded and the wraiths warded against are covered. Two things worth knowing: "ground" is recorded as a property of the feathers, so "ground up" and "lying on the ground" are not distinguished, and the rule only fires for feathers still registered as belonging to a sky-cat — which the gathered feathers of the previous sentence are not.
